description:
Beyond the stars. Beyond the ordinary.

We are a team of innovators pushing the boundaries of space exploration through NASA-powered data, intelligent hazard tracking, and advanced quantum-inspired routing. Our mission is to transform complex cosmic information into smarter, safer navigation — because the future of exploration begins beyond the known.
summary:
DAPS – Deep Space Archival and Positioning System

DAPS is a project designed to explore how technology can make space exploration safer and more efficient. We developed an interactive website that brings together space data, hazard tracking, route planning, and interesting visualisations in one place which is the main aim of the challenge.

Our project uses NASA's space-weather data to show information about solar activity and possible space hazards. It also includes simulated hazards and route-planning features to demonstrate how technology could help us understand the challenges of travelling through space.

DAPS aims to make complex space information easier to understand and explore. It shows how scientific research, technology, and creative thinking can work together to solve problems that may affect future space missions.

We believe this project is important because space exploration is becoming more advanced, and understanding the risks involved is essential. Through DAPS, we hope to encourage new ideas and inspire people to think about the future of space exploration.
details:
DAPS (Deep Space Archival and Positioning System) is an interactive website developed to explore how technology can make space exploration smarter, safer and more efficient. It brings together features such as route planning, hazard tracking, space visualisation and space-weather information. Users can select destinations, choose different travel speeds and explore possible routes while learning about potential space hazards.

The project uses NASA's DONKI data to display information about real space-weather events, while simulated data is used for the hazard visualisations. We developed the website using HTML, CSS and JavaScript, with Node.js to support the NASA API connection.

What makes DAPS creative is the way it combines different scientific and technological concepts into one interactive platform, including quantum-inspired routing. It makes complex space-related information easier to explore and understand. While developing the project, our team considered scientific accuracy, user-friendliness, creativity, functionality and future improvements. Our aim is to encourage interest in space science and demonstrate how innovation and technology could contribute to the future of space exploration.
